source.note: Scan without a text layer. National Senior Certificate paper (cover: NATIONAL SENIOR CERTIFICATE; running header: NSC). The PDF includes the cover (printed page 1), the instructions (page 2) and the information sheet (page 11); PDF page n = printed page n. The cover states that the question paper consists of 10 pages and 1 information sheet. Duration 3 hours as printed on the cover. Source file and hash are recorded in sources/maths/manifest.json.

extraction.method: manual transcription from 170 dpi page renders, checked at 400 dpi where needed

questions.text_md: $3x^{2}-2x=14$ (correct to TWO decimal places)
Solve for $x$: $(x-1)(x-2)<6$

The roots of a quadratic equation are:  $x=\dfrac{3\pm\sqrt{-k-4}}{2}$

For which values of $k$ are the roots real?
Write down the fourth term of the series.
Calculate the $251^{\text{st}}$ term of the series.
Express the series in sigma notation.
Calculate the sum of the series.
How many terms in the series are divisible by $4$?
questions.notes: Count of terms in an AP that are divisible by 4. Closest existing skills tagged.

questions.text_md: Write down the value of $p$.
Determine the $n^{\text{th}}$ term of the sequence.
The first difference between two consecutive terms of the sequence is $96$. Calculate the values of these two terms.

questions.stem_md: The first three terms of a geometric sequence are:  $16\,;\,4\,;\,1$

questions.text_md: Calculate the value of the $12^{\text{th}}$ term. (Leave your answer in simplified exponential form.)
Calculate the sum of the first $10$ terms of the sequence.
Determine the value of:  $\left(1+\dfrac{1}{2}\right)\left(1+\dfrac{1}{3}\right)\left(1+\dfrac{1}{4}\right)\left(1+\dfrac{1}{5}\right)\ldots$  up to $98$ factors.
questions.notes: Telescoping product of 98 factors of the form $(1+1/n)$. No dedicated skill; closest existing skill tagged.

questions.stem_md: The diagram below shows the hyperbola $g$ defined by  $g(x)=\dfrac{2}{x+p}+q$  with asymptotes $y=1$ and $x=-1$. The graph of $g$ intersects the $x$-axis at $\mathrm{T}$ and the $y$-axis at $(0\,;\,3)$. The line $y=x$ intersects the hyperbola in the first quadrant at $\mathrm{S}$.

questions.text_md: Write down the values of $p$ and $q$.
Calculate the $x$-coordinate of $\mathrm{T}$.
Write down the equation of the vertical asymptote of the graph of $h$, if $h(x)=g(x+5)$
Calculate the length of $\mathrm{OS}$.
For which values of $k$ will the equation $g(x)=x+k$ have two real roots that are of opposite signs?
questions.notes: Two real roots of opposite signs for $g(x)=x+k$. Closest existing skill tagged.

questions.stem_md: Given: $f(x)=\log_{a}x$ where $a>0$. $\mathrm{S}\left(\dfrac{1}{3}\,;\,-1\right)$ is a point on the graph of $f$.

questions.text_md: Prove that $a=3$.
Write down the equation of $h$, the inverse of $f$, in the form $y=\ldots$
If $g(x)=-f(x)$, determine the equation of $g$.
Write down the domain of $g$.
Determine the values of $x$ for which $f(x)\geq-3$.

questions.stem_md: Given: $g(x)=4x^{2}-6$ and $f(x)=2\sqrt{x}$. The graphs of $g$ and $f$ are sketched below. $\mathrm{S}$ is an $x$-intercept of $g$ and $\mathrm{K}$ is a point between $\mathrm{O}$ and $\mathrm{S}$. The straight line $\mathrm{QKT}$ with $\mathrm{Q}$ on the graph of $f$ and $\mathrm{T}$ on the graph of $g$, is parallel to the $y$-axis.

questions.text_md: Determine the $x$-coordinate of $\mathrm{S}$, correct to TWO decimal places.
Write down the coordinates of the turning point of $g$.
Write down the length of $\mathrm{QKT}$ in terms of $x$, where $x$ is the $x$-coordinate of $\mathrm{K}$.
Calculate the maximum length of $\mathrm{QT}$.

Exactly five years ago Mpume bought a new car for R$145\,000$. The current book value of this car is R$72\,500$. If the car depreciates by a fixed annual rate according to the reducing-balance method, calculate the rate of depreciation.

questions.stem_md: Samuel took out a home loan for R$500\,000$ at an interest rate of $12\%$ per annum, compounded monthly. He plans to repay this loan over $20$ years and his first payment is made one month after the loan is granted.

questions.text_md: Calculate the value of Samuel's monthly instalment.

Melissa took out a loan for the same amount and at the same interest rate as Samuel. Melissa decided to pay R$6\,000$ at the end of every month. Calculate how many months it took for Melissa to settle the loan.
Who pays more interest, Samuel or Melissa? Justify your answer.
Determine $f'(x)$ from first principles if $f(x)=x^{3}$.
Determine the derivative of: $f(x)=2x^{2}+\dfrac{1}{2}x^{4}-3$
questions.notes: Exponent on the second term confirmed at higher resolution as $x^{4}$.

questions.text_md: If $y=(x^{6}-1)^{2}$, prove that $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=12x^{5}\sqrt{y}$, if $x>1$.
Given: $f(x)=2x^{3}-2x^{2}+4x-1$. Determine the interval on which $f$ is concave up.
Calculate the coordinates of the turning points of the graph of $f$.
Sketch the graph of $f$, clearly indicating the intercepts with the axes and the turning points.
For which value(s) of $x$ will $x.f'(x)<0$?
questions.notes: Printed as $x.f'(x)<0$ (the product of $x$ and $f'(x)$), confirmed at 400 dpi. Closest existing skill tagged.

questions.stem_md: A box is made from a rectangular piece of cardboard, $100$ cm by $40$ cm, by cutting out the shaded areas and folding along the dotted lines as shown in the diagram above.

questions.text_md: Express the length $l$ in terms of the height $h$.
Hence prove that the volume of the box is given by $V=h(50-h)(40-2h)$
For which value of $h$ will the volume of the box be a maximum?

questions.stem_md:
A survey concerning their holiday preferences was done with $180$ staff members. The options they could choose from were to:

* Go to the coast
* Visit a game park
* Stay at home

The results were recorded in the table below:

table.caption: Holiday preferences of 180 staff members, by gender

questions.stem_md: Determine the probability that a randomly selected staff member:

questions.text_md: Is male
Does not prefer visiting a game park
Are the events 'being a male' and 'staying at home' independent events? Motivate your answer with relevant calculations.

questions.stem_md: A password consists of five different letters of the English alphabet. Each letter may be used only once. How many passwords can be formed if:

questions.text_md: All the letters of the alphabet can be used
The password must start with a 'D' and end with an 'L'

questions.stem_md: Seven cars of different manufacturers, of which $3$ are silver, are to be parked in a straight line.

questions.text_md: In how many different ways can ALL the cars be parked?
If the three silver cars must be parked next to each other, determine in how many different ways the cars can be parked.

figures.caption: Hyperbola $g(x)=\dfrac{2}{x+p}+q$ with asymptotes $y=1$ and $x=-1$, $y$-intercept $3$, $x$-intercept $\mathrm{T}$, and the line $y=x$ meeting $g$ in the first quadrant at $\mathrm{S}$.
figures.notes: Both branches of g are labelled. The vertical asymptote is a dotted line through x=-1; the horizontal asymptote is a dotted line labelled 1.

figures.caption: Graph of $f(x)=\log_{a}x$, $a>0$, passing through $\mathrm{S}\left(\dfrac{1}{3}\,;\,-1\right)$.
figures.notes: The curve is drawn only for x>0, with arrows at both ends, and is labelled f. The x-intercept at 1 is shown but not labelled.

figures.caption: Parabola $g(x)=4x^{2}-6$ and $f(x)=2\sqrt{x}$. $\mathrm{S}$ is the positive $x$-intercept of $g$. $\mathrm{K}$ lies on the $x$-axis between $\mathrm{O}$ and $\mathrm{S}$. The vertical line $\mathrm{QKT}$ meets $f$ at $\mathrm{Q}$ and $g$ at $\mathrm{T}$.
figures.notes: A right-angle mark is shown at K. K, Q and T are illustrative positions between O and S; their exact x-coordinate is not a given value. The turning point of g at (0; -6) is drawn but not labelled.

figures.caption: An unlabelled rectangular box (left) and the net of a $100$ cm by $40$ cm piece of cardboard (right). The net is partitioned into a top row of height $h$, a middle row of height $l$ and a bottom row of height $h$, and along the base into widths $h$, $b$, $h$ and $b$. Shaded rectangles (top-left $h\times h$, top-right covering the last two columns, bottom-left $h\times h$, and bottom-right covering the last two columns) are cut out; dotted lines in the middle row are fold lines.

spec.scene: Left: perspective sketch of a closed rectangular box, no labels. Right: rectangular net 100 cm wide by 40 cm tall, with rows h, l, h and columns h, b, h, b.
spec.animation_hint: Show the shaded rectangles being cut out and the remaining net folding along the dotted lines into the box.

figures.notes: Schematic, not to scale. The 3D box has no dimensions. l and b are to be expressed in terms of h.
